notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the sources failed: the tool said I had no code-execution calls left for this turn, and that tool is the only way I can reach the web. So I haven't read any pages on Psalm 33.

Your rules say to report only what I actually read and give a URL for every point. Since I read nothing, I've left out all verse notes rather than writing them from memory.

These are the pages I tried to open first. Some of the addresses are my best guesses and haven't been checked:
- **Traditional verse-by-verse:** enduringword.com (David Guzik on Psalm 33), preceptaustin.org's Psalm 33 commentary, and biblehub.com's Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Clarke and Wesley notes on Psalm 33.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** newadvent.org, where Augustine's exposition of this psalm is listed as Psalm 32, because older Greek and Latin Bibles number the Psalms differently.
- **Next:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, the netbible.org notes, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, and a search of desiringgod.org, ligonier.org and thegospelcoalition.org for sermons on particular verses, especially vv. 6, 9 and 12. Then I'd check whether any of the sites discuss prosperity or word-of-faith readings of vv. 16–19.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start with those pages and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point, leaving out anything I can't find.
